service.name: Live music and a DJ for a Halloween party
service.serviceType: A DJ, a party band or live band karaoke for adult Halloween parties at home and at venues
service.description: A DJ, a party band or live band karaoke for an adult Halloween party across Denver and the Front Range, at home or at a venue: a DJ in 6 by 4 feet playing the songs a costume crowd wants, a trio or quartet playing the hits to a floor, or the band that plays the 80s and 90s hits and hands the microphone to anyone in costume, with sound support sized to the house and one personal contact for the night.

faqs.q: Do you have a DJ for a Halloween party?
faqs.a: Yes. A DJ is the usual first question for a Halloween party, and it's the easiest one for a house: a booth in 6 by 4 feet on one dedicated circuit, a 45-minute load-in, and a set built around the decade your guests grew up in with the songs that have to happen placed where you want them. It's one contract with sound support sized to the house, and the same DJ can take the late end of a night after a band.

faqs.q: What does a DJ or a band for a Halloween party cost?
faqs.a: What live music costs in this market is set out on our pricing page, and two posts cover the two halves of this question: what a DJ costs in Denver, and whether a band or a DJ is the right call for the night. Send us the date and a sentence about the house and we'll come back with a configuration and a price for that night rather than a range.

faqs.q: Is live band karaoke a good Halloween party idea?
faqs.a: It's the one people tell stories about afterward. The band plays the 80s and 90s hits on its own, sung out front, and hands the microphone to anyone in costume who wants a song, with the words on a screen and a host keeping a sign-up list on paper, so nobody has to sing for the night to work and the crowd gets through six to ten songs an hour. The four-piece with its host and two lyric screens takes 14 by 10 feet and two dedicated circuits, so it wants a big main floor, a finished basement or a garage with the cars out.

faqs.q: When is Halloween 2026, and how far ahead should we book?
faqs.a: Halloween 2026 falls on Saturday, October 31, so the whole city parties on the same night, and the Saturday before it, October 24, is the other night people throw the party. Send us whichever date is yours as soon as you have it, and we'll check the booking calendar and come back with a configuration and a price for that night.

faqs.q: Will the band or the DJ play in costume?
faqs.a: Ask us with the booking. The musicians decide what they wear, and a themed set, the songs that belong to the night, is a request we take with the date. What every booking includes regardless is an announcement microphone, so a costume contest can be run from the band's sound system rather than over it.

faqs.q: How late can a Halloween party at home run with live music?
faqs.a: The loud part of any home party belongs indoors once the neighbors have gone to bed, and the rules vary by street and by HOA, so we don't quote an ordinance. The planning fact is enough: a Halloween party runs late, so its floor is usually a finished basement, a garage with the cars out, or the main floor with the doors shut. If your street or HOA has quiet hours in writing, give them to us at contract and the night gets built under them.

faqs.q: How much space does a Halloween party band need?
faqs.a: A DJ takes 6 by 4 feet on one dedicated circuit, a trio 12 by 8 on one, and a quartet or the live band karaoke four-piece 14 by 10 on two, and none of them want to share a circuit with the fog machine and the string lights. Sets run 45 to 60 minutes with music through the breaks, so the party never goes quiet. Footprints for every size are on the technical page.

faqs.q: Do you play office Halloween parties?
faqs.a: Yes. The Friday-before version at work books the same three configurations, a DJ, a party band or live band karaoke, and the corporate page covers how a band works around a program and what a venue needs to know.
